notes: Topline: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing chat + rerank pipelines (personalization layer) — procurement cycle accelerated by Q2 marketing push.
Primary ask from infra: firm throughput guarantees (min tokens/sec), concurrency caps per-tenant, and well-defined burst policy (how many tokens/min allowed above baseline).
Latency SLO: product team wants 95th pct chat response <250ms for 512-token avg responses; infra wants P99 <500ms for peak load. Legal pushing for P99 SLA language + credits formula.

POC summary: ran 48h PoC on hosted with autoscale — avg 9k t/s sustained, spikes to 28k t/s for short bursts; they want a dedicated pool that guarantees 12k t/s sustained with burst to 40k t/s for 3 minutes.
Quote from Head of Infra: "We need hard concurrency caps per customer and a documented backpressure/fallback flow (model degradation fallback to cheaper quantized variant)."
Budget: prefer predictable monthly committed spend (reserved GPUs) rather than big overage exposure; finance target ARR band noted above, expects 12–18 month payback on infra uplift.
Security: SSO + enterprise SAML mandatory; retention and residency for EU customers — default VPC deployment with optional on-prem carrier for PHI-adjacent flows.
SE note: workload mix = 60% chat (low-latency), 30% rerank (batched high-throughput), 10% embeddings (bulk offline). Batching knobs matter for cost; want Redwood Optimize recommendations in contract.

Key negotiation points: 1) minimum tokens/sec guarantee and measurement window; 2) concurrency caps vs per-tenant throughput mapping; 3) burst policy (duration, throttling algorithm, billing for bursts); 4) reserved GPU equivalence and scaling plan; 5) SLA credits calculation (need examples).
Ask from procurement: show 3 sample SLA clauses with numerical examples (credit calc) + runbook for incident where Dedicated capacity exhausted and routing to fallback model in another region.
Won't do: customer is hesitant about fully air-gapped solution initially; may revisit after SOC2/ISO if contract >$1M.
SE action items: size dedicated pool equivalent to ~8 x A100-80GB (estimate) for target 12k sustained t/s, validate kernel/kernel-selection for their 8k token context staging tests.
Customer success concern: need per-route token cost breakdown in Console and alerting on regression vs baseline prompts — tied to Redwood Optimize deliverables.
Short quote from Product Lead on 2026-02-28 call: "We will not ship the new personalization feature until latency is predictable under peak events."

Negotiation posture: Vertex prefers committed baseline that covers 85% of expected demand, with clearly priced bursts; Redwood suggested canary/burst tiers — vendor to provide formal burst SLA options.
